nodes.name: Monthly (2nd, 07:00)
nodes.notes: SHIPS DISABLED. Enable only after a parallel month — run the pipeline alongside the manual process and compare every number first (HANDOFF_AUTOMATION.md, "Run it a month early").

nodes.name: Webhook
nodes.notes: POST /webhook/rbl-month with {"month":"2026-08","dryRun":true}. Attach a Header Auth credential in n8n — this endpoint starts a run that writes to the database.

nodes.name: Resolve month
nodes.notes: month = webhook body → $vars.RBL_MONTH → last month. Mints the runId and publishes month/runId into execution.customData for the Error Handler.

nodes.name: Acquire the month lock
nodes.notes: One of only two Execute Command nodes allowed here (§3.2). Exit 10 = another run holds it. The command is wrapped so the shell always exits 0 and the real code travels in stdout as __EXIT__<code>. Measured on n8n 2.35.7: this node reports exitCode ONLY when the command exits 0 — on any non-zero exit it emits { error } alone, dropping both exitCode and stdout, with the stderr text as the message. That makes an exit 10 (a human must decide) indistinguishable from a crash, and loses the JSON line the contract is built on. onError:continueRegularOutput keeps the workflow running but does not restore the fields.

nodes.name: Lock acquired?
nodes.notes: False means another run has this month. That path notifies WITHOUT releasing — the lock is not ours to release.

nodes.name: 00 · Preflight
nodes.notes: Runs stage 00 through RBL · Stage Runner and returns the envelope. No Execute Command here — the orchestrator owns no shell but lock/unlock.

nodes.name: 00 ok?
nodes.notes: done → next stage. stop or crash → halt, release the lock, notify.

nodes.name: 02 ok?
nodes.notes: done → next stage. stop or crash → halt, release the lock, notify.

nodes.name: 06 ok?
nodes.notes: done → next stage. stop or crash → halt, release the lock, notify.

nodes.notes: Runs stage 07 through RBL · Stage Runner and returns the envelope. No Execute Command here — the orchestrator owns no shell but lock/unlock.

nodes.name: Cohorts (03 + 04)
nodes.notes: Fans out one row per uncollected cohort, retries a crash 3 times with 5/10/20-minute backoff, escalates and continues. Returns monthIncomplete.

nodes.name: All cohorts collected?
nodes.notes: False → skip stages 05-07 entirely. A month missing a cohort must not be built.

nodes.name: Explain the halt
nodes.notes: stop → amber "awaiting a decision". crash → red. The distinction is preserved end to end: exit code, branch, colour, wording.

nodes.name: Release the lock
nodes.notes: Runs on EVERY exit path that took the lock — success and halt alike (§3.2 step 13). A crash path is covered by RBL · Error Handler, which releases it too. That makes an exit 10 (a human must decide) indistinguishable from a crash, and loses the JSON line the contract is built on. onError:continueRegularOutput keeps the workflow running but does not restore the fields.

parameters.content:
## Stages 03 + 04 run inside `RBL · Cohort Loop`

One row per uncollected cohort, so a stall is visible **while it is happening** rather than after two hours of silence.

Retry lives there, not here: a crash gets 3 attempts at 5 / 10 / 20 minutes; a stop escalates immediately in amber. A cohort that never collects is marked **failed** in state — never read downstream as "no calls".

If any cohort fails, `monthIncomplete` comes back true and **stages 05-07 are skipped**.

nodes.name: Stop or crash?
nodes.notes: A stop is a question for a human — it gets a form. A crash is a fault — it halts.

parameters.jsCode:
/* Turn a stage's stop payload into a form the operator can answer.

   THE INFERENCE IS SHOWN BUT NEVER PRE-FILLED. plan_month's campaign guess is
   right most of the time, and "most of the time" is exactly the failure this
   stop exists to prevent: CYC 18 PDD+7 and CYC 20 PDD+5 are real August Bucket
   books that the inference calls PreX (PIPELINE_BUILD_RESULT.md finding #1). A
   form that arrives pre-filled with the guess can be accepted with one click by
   someone who never read it, which is the same thing as not asking. So the
   campaign field starts EMPTY, with the inference printed beside it, and
   --apply-assignments refuses an entry that does not name one. */

const env = $input.first().json;
const r = $('Resolve month').first().json;
const j = env.json ?? {};
const isPlan = env.stage === '02';

const rows = isPlan
  ? (j.unassigned ?? []).map((u) => ({
      book: u.book,
      loadDate: u.loadDate,
      _inference: u.inference ?? null,
      _why: u.reason,
      campaign: '',
      days: u.needs === 'days' ? '' : undefined,
    }))
  : (j.unresolvedGaps ?? j.gaps ?? []).map((g) => ({
      book: g.book,
      _gap: g.reason + (g.dates ? ' — missing ' + g.dates.join(', ') : ''),
      ruling: '',
      reason: '',
    }));

const heading = isPlan
  ? 'Campaign assignment — ' + rows.length + ' book(s) need a decision'
  : 'Gap rulings — ' + rows.length + ' book(s) could not be fully assembled';

const guidance = isPlan
  ? [
      'For each book set "campaign" to prex or bucket. "_inference" is what',
      'plan_month guessed from the name — it is shown, not applied, because it',
      'is wrong for real books: CYC 18 PDD+7 and CYC 20 PDD+5 are Bucket books',
      'it calls PreX. Set "days" only where the field is present and empty.',
      '',
      'Campaign decides which status file a book is paired with, and the two',
      'campaigns use different outcome vocabularies. Pair a book with the wrong',
      'one and every number on the report renders, and every number is wrong.',
    ].join('\n')
  : [
      'For each book set "ruling" to one of:',
      '  build-partial  build the days that exist, knowing the report is short',
      '  wait-for-file  the file is still coming — this keeps the run blocked',
      '  exclude-book   this book is not part of this month\'s reporting',
      '',
      'A "reason" is required on every row. State answers which books were',
      'partial; only you can answer why one shipped that way.',
    ].join('\n');

return [{
  json: {
    ...r,
    stage: env.stage,
    formHeading: heading,
    formGuidance: guidance,
    prefill: JSON.stringify(rows, null, 2),
    rowCount: rows.length,
    severity: 'stop',
    title: isPlan ? 'campaign assignment needed' : 'gap rulings needed',
    body: heading + '\n\n' + (isPlan
      ? rows.map((x) => '  ' + x.book + '  loaded ' + x.loadDate + '  (inference: ' + (x._inference ?? 'none') + ')').join('\n')
      : rows.map((x) => '  ' + x.book + '  ' + x._gap).join('\n')),
  },
}];

nodes.name: Build the question
nodes.notes: Renders the stop payload into form rows. The campaign inference is SHOWN but never pre-filled — a form that can be accepted with one click is the same as not asking.

nodes.name: Ask (amber, with the resume link)
nodes.notes: Carries $execution.resumeUrl — the difference between "a decision is needed" and "someone must go and find where to make it".

nodes.name: Wait for the decision
nodes.notes: 48-hour deadline with a defined timeout path. An execution waiting forever is how a queue silently fills.

nodes.name: Record the decision
nodes.notes: Writes the answer with decidedBy/decidedAt into state/ AND re-runs the stage in the same invocation. The repo is the audit record, not n8n. The command is wrapped so the shell always exits 0 and the real code travels in stdout as __EXIT__<code>. Measured on n8n 2.35.7: this node reports exitCode ONLY when the command exits 0 — on any non-zero exit it emits { error } alone, dropping both exitCode and stdout, with the stderr text as the message. That makes an exit 10 (a human must decide) indistinguishable from a crash, and loses the JSON line the contract is built on. onError:continueRegularOutput keeps the workflow running but does not restore the fields.

nodes.name: 08 · Client portfolios
nodes.notes: Refuses to run unless stage 07 passed — a client-facing document built on unverified numbers is the worst output this system can produce.

nodes.name: Deliver
nodes.notes: Builds the delivery message and names the client PDFs as attachments. The only notification that carries files.
